numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For the special stdtr wrapper logic, when df is -inf the wrapper returns the value from the normal instead of nan (because the infinity shortcut was applied to any inf).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Return nan when df is -inf rather than taking the normal/ndtr shortcut result.
trigger_conditions: the code reaches the infinity shortcut controlled by `if isinf(df)` in the buggy version (fixed to `if isinf(df) and df > 0`).

oracle_clues: PR/commit message: "Ensure that -inf returns nan rather than the value from a normal"
PR body: "Changes inf check from any inf to only positive inf. -inf is not passed to function to get the correct result of `nan`"
diff evidence (stdtr): changed from `if isinf(df): return NAN if isnan(t) else ndtr(t)` to `if isinf(df) and df > 0: ...`
diff evidence (stdtrit): changed from `if isinf(df): return NAN if isnan(p) else ndtri(p)` to `if isinf(df) and df > 0: ...`

Issue example: `from scipy.stats import norm; from scipy.special import nrdtrimn; x, mu, sigma = 0, 0, 0.1; q = norm.cdf(x, loc=mu, scale=sigma)  # 0.5; nrdtrimn(q, x, sigma) -> NaN; I expected ... mu (mu=0)`

category_specific_evidence: Special values involved: -inf (negative infinity) in the df argument to special stdtr/stdtrit functions.
The incorrect behavior being fixed: -inf was treated as +inf and values from the normal were returned.
The correct handling required: return NaN for -inf rather than the value from a normal.
Code change evidence: wrapper changed the infinity check from `if isinf(df)` to `if isinf(df) and df > 0` for both `stdtr` and `stdtrit`.
Test evidence for correct behavior: `assert np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtr(-np.inf, [-np.inf, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, np.inf])))` and `assert np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtrit(-np.inf, [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0])))`.
Correct handling rationale from PR description: “Changes inf check from any inf to only positive inf. -inf is not passed to function to get the correct result of `nan`”.
Implementation detail evidence: `return NAN if isnan(t) else ndtr(t)` / `return NAN if isnan(p) else ndtri(p)` occurs only when `df` is positive infinity after the fix (`isinf(df) and df > 0`).

Return nan when df is -inf (negative infinity), rather than taking the normal/inverse-normal shortcut result. The wrapper was changed from "if isinf(df)" to "if isinf(df) and df > 0" so that only +inf follows the shortcut while -inf falls through to nan handling.
